title: Proper morphisms of algebraic spaces are preserved by base change
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is quasi-compact if for every affine scheme $T$ mapping to its target its pullback to $T$ is a quasi-compact algebraic space, meaning that it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion: every scheme base change of that diagonal is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Locally of finite type is tested on compatible etale scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and finite type means locally of finite type and quasi-compact. Universally closed means that every algebraic-space base change is closed on point spaces. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed (the scheme convention is [def-weil-proper-morphism]). If $f$ is proper, then the projection $f':X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ is proper. No Noetherian, finite-presentation, or representability hypothesis on $f$ or $g$ is required.

proof.text: Put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, $H=X\times_Y X$ and $H'=X'\times_{Y'}X'$, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The projections $X'\to X$ induce $H'\to H$. For a scheme $T\to H'$, write its coordinates as $(x_1,x_2,y')$, with $f(x_1)=f(x_2)=g(y')$. On every test scheme $U$, a section of $X\times_H T$ is $(x,t)$ with $x=x_1(t)=x_2(t)$. Send it to $((x,y'(t)),t)$ in $X'\times_{H'}T$. Conversely forget the $Y'$-coordinate. These formulas are inverse, natural in $U$, and over $T$, so they identify the two sheaf projections. The former is represented by a scheme closed immersion by separatedness of $f$; hence the latter is too. Every scheme test of the diagonal of $f'$ is therefore a closed immersion, proving separatedness.

proof.text: Properness gives that $f$ is of finite type. In [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], use both arbitrary-base-change preservation and the explicit agreement with ordinary algebraic-space notions. Algebraic spaces are the discrete-groupoid cases of the stack conventions in that statement, so it applies to $X,Y,Y'$ and arbitrary $g$. It yields finite type of $f'$, including both quasi-compactness and local finite type. The scheme-test quasi-compactness convention fixed in the statement is precisely the current convention of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]; its locality theorem is not needed.

source.place: Tag 03XH, lemma-base-change-finite-type; the existing input also states the more general stack version (stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06FU) and its algebraic-space compatibility

proof.text: For any algebraic space $T$ with a morphism $h:T\to Y'$, the sheaf fibre-product universal property gives $(X\times_Y Y')\times_{Y'}T\cong X\times_Y T$, where $T\to Y$ is $g\circ h$: both sides classify a section $x$ of $X$ and a section $t$ of $T$ with $f(x)=g(h(t))$. The projections to $T$ agree. The right-hand projection is closed on point spaces because $f$ is universally closed. Consequently every base change of $f'$ is closed, as required. Write $a:A\to C$ for the displayed isomorphism. For a subset $V\subseteq|C|$ and any etale scheme chart $u:U\to A$, the inverse image of $|a|^{-1}(V)$ under $|u|$ equals the inverse image of $V$ under $|a\circ u|$. Composition with $a$ and with its inverse bijects these charts, so the final-topology definition [def-a1-space-point-topology] says $|a|^{-1}(V)$ is open exactly when $V$ is open. Thus $|a|$ is a homeomorphism and the closedness conclusion follows.
Steps 1, 2 and 3 give respectively separatedness, finite type and universal closedness of $f'$. Their conjunction is the stated definition of properness, proving the assertion.
